title: Metrics Access Sanitizer and Permission Hints for Cross-Org Usage Exports
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our analytics export endpoints and tenant-level usage views are currently permissive at the aggregate level and expose metric names/labels that can reveal sensitive information for multi-tenant customers (e.g., custom route names, internal feature flags, or resource identifiers). This ticket introduces a pragmatic authorization + sanitization layer ("Metrics Access Sanitizer") at the analytics service boundary and a lightweight permission hint field in usage responses to enable downstream clients (console, exports, BI jobs) to apply least-privilege filtering without re-running full entitlement checks.
acceptance_criteria: A Metrics Access Sanitizer middleware enforces per-tenant allowed_metric_patterns and forbidden_metric_patterns when serving aggregated usage views.
Usage endpoints include an optional permission_hints array that lists canonical metric identifiers the caller may request for deeper detail.
Export pipeline transforms (materialized views and job-layer filters) respect the sanitizer rules and redact metric labels flagged as sensitive.
End-to-end tests covering common complex cases: cross-tenant joins, derived metrics, and historical exports; no regressions in existing dashboards.
Performance overhead on 95th percentile query latency <= 8% for typical dashboards (verified in staging).
Security review completed and sign-off from InfoSec with threat model updated.
technical_notes: Design: introduce a lightweight AuthorizationHints interface in the analytics gateway that returns 'permission_hints' (list of metric keys) alongside existing result metadata. These hints are computed from the entitlements cache and the requested metric selector before heavy query execution.

Sanitizer: rule set stored in the Entitlement service with two lists per tenant: allowed_metric_patterns (globs) and forbidden_metric_patterns. Resolution order: explicit allow > explicit deny > default-deny for sensitive namespaces.

Query flow changes: analytics-gateway -> entitlement-check (fast cache) -> compute permission_hints -> rewrite query to exclude forbidden metrics OR substitute redacted placeholder metrics in the projection.

Pipeline changes: Add a transform stage in the daily export job to map forbidden metric labels to '<redacted_metric>' and drop sensitive label dimensions when exports are requested by non-admin roles.

DB: Create a small, indexed mapping table analytics_metric_metadata(metric_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, sensitivity VARCHAR, canonical_name TEXT) used by sanitizer. Migration job will backfill from model_catalog and existing dashboards.
Cache: permission_hints are cached per (tenant_id, role_hash) for 60s, invalidated on entitlement updates via pub/sub.
Compatibility: Default behavior for tenants without explicit rules remains unchanged; admins can opt into strict mode via tenant settings.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy sanitizer behind feature flag 'metrics-sanitizer' for internal tenants. Run export smoke tests and gathering latency traces.
Phase 2 (canary): Enable for 10% of production tenants with low volume. Monitor failed exports, missing metrics, and support tickets.
Phase 3 (gradual): Ramp to all tenants with strict mode off. Provide migration helpers and UI for admins to see redacted metrics.
Phase 4 (strict): After 2 weeks of stability, enable strict mode for security-sensitive customers and onboard tenant-specific rules.
Rollback: Feature flag toggle and ability to bypass sanitizer for emergency operational access (audit-logged).
testing_plan: Unit tests for AuthorizationHints computation with permutations of role sets and metric patterns.
Integration tests: analytics-gateway + entitlement-cache + metric_metadata table. Verify query rewrites produce expected redaction.
E2E: Create a synthetic tenant in staging with intentionally sensitive labels; run full export and verify redaction and permission_hints correctness.
Perf: Load test with real dashboard workloads in staging to validate <8% P95 latency change (compare baseline trace IDs).
Security: Automated fuzzing to ensure no metric label leakage on join/aggregate edge cases.
monitoring: New metrics: sanitizer.requests_total, sanitizer.redactions_total, sanitizer.hint_cache_hits, sanitizer.hint_cache_misses.
Alerts: redactions_total spike > 10x baseline for a tenant triggers ops review; hint_cache_miss_rate > 5% triggers cache tuning.
Dashboards: per-tenant redaction counts, average extra planning time for queries (ms), latency impact percentiles.
Audit logs: every redaction and bypass decision emits an audit event with actor, tenant_id, metric_key, and reason.
